Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the draft DPA and sent over Annex B redlines (attached). A few high-level items we need to resolve before Legal will sign:

- Residency: We need confirmation that customer data for our EU users will be processed and stored in the EU. Prefer explicit EU-only residency language for any personal data.
- Retention: ProspectCo requires a 7-year retention option for customer records originating in our systems (we understand logs may be different).
- Deletion and certification: We want a clause requiring deletion upon termination and a written deletion certificate within 30 days.
- Subprocessors & KMS: Need a current subprocessors list and confirmation that Redwood supports KMS/HSM key control or BYOK for sensitive data.

Attached: ProspectCo_DPA_redlines_20260210.pdf (redlines + comments). Can you advise which of these Redwood can accept as-is and where we should expect a counter?

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA Annex B: Data residency & retention

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. I ran this by product/security and here are Redwood's initial positions so we can align quickly:

1) Residency
- Hosted API (default): processing occurs in region assigned to the customer — we have EU regions (Frankfurt/Amsterdam) but some control-plane functions remain US-based.
- Dedicated & Private: Redwood can commit to EU-only processing and storage (customer-controlled VPC / on-prem) via Annex B when Dedicated or Private deployment is chosen.

2) Retention
- Default: token-level request/response content is retained for up to 90 days for troubleshooting and model quality.
- Logs & audit data: retained 365 days by default.
- Backups/snapshots: retained up to 14 days.
- We cannot agree to open-ended 7-year retention as a default; however, we can support custom retention settings for Dedicated/Private customers and discuss contractual add-ons for longer-term archival (subject to encryption and storage costs).

3) Deletion & certification
- We can support deletion of customer data on request and will purge active data sets within 30 days of verified request.
- Certification: Redwood can provide a deletion attestation within 45 days after completion (covers primary data stores and known backups; immutable audit records are handled per policy).

4) Subprocessors & KMS
- We will provide an up-to-date subprocessors list and commit to notifying you of material changes.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-supplied key management (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted API customers can opt into HSM-backed keys with contractual SLAs.

I'll draft proposed Annex B language reflecting the above and share a redline by Thursday. If any of the above is a hard blocker for ProspectCo (e.g., 7-year retention as a mandatory requirement on hosted), flag it now and we can loop in Security + Legal for escalation.

Thanks — Neha

Folks — forwarding ProspectCo's follow-ups. Key asks: deletion attestation within 30 days, explicit enumeration of control-plane metadata flows, and current subprocessors list.

Quick proposed negotiation posture:
- Offer: Deletion attestation within 45 days (we explained 45 above). If Legal pushes hard for 30 days, offer 30 days for Dedicated/Private only; 45 days for hosted.
- Control-plane: provide a short catalog of metadata types (e.g., request headers, timestamps, region identifiers) and a statement that we do not surface PII in control-plane logs. Security should sign off on the wording.
- Subprocessors: provide current list + commit to 30 days' notice for material changes.

Any objections? If not, I'll draft the Annex B redline and a deletion attestation template.

Neha — OK to proceed with your posture. Two small asks from Security:

1) Deletion attestation: security prefers "within 45 days" language but accepts 30 for Dedicated/Private. Include a short appendix describing which stores are purged (primary DBs, cache layers, and backup snapshot policy).

2) Control-plane metadata: include a clear list and an explicit statement that control-plane metadata is pseudonymized and not customer PII; provide examples: region code, API route, timestamp, request size. Avoid saying "no PII" in absolute terms; prefer "we do not intentionally store customer PII in control-plane services."

I will attach the subprocessors list (current) under separate cover; legal can consume that.

— Vivek
Director, Security Engineering

Subject: RE: DPA Annex B: residency & retention questions — proposed redline

Hi Samantha — based on the internal review, attached is our proposed Annex B redline and a deletion attestation template. Highlights:

- Residency: explicit EU-only processing for customer data when customer elects Dedicated or Private deployment. For hosted customers, we will route processing to EU region where requested; control-plane orchestration may transit the US.

- Retention: default hosted retention kept at 90 days (tokens) and 365 days (logs). For Dedicated/Private customers we will include configurable retention up to 7 years as an add-on.

- Deletion attestation: Redwood will remove or irreversibly overwrite customer data from primary and backup stores and provide an attestation within 45 days for hosted customers and within 30 days for Dedicated/Private customers. Attestation language is in the attachment.

- Subprocessors & KMS: subprocessors list is attached; we commit to 30 days' notice for material changes and BYOK/KMS support on Dedicated/Private.

Next steps: if this is acceptable, please confirm and we'll prepare the Annex B redline in the master DPA for signature and route the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — Neha
